heroText: Ottawa is a Canada base best planned around named sights rather than a generic stopover. Start with Parliament Hill, add Rideau Canal, and use ByWard Market to understand the city's history, street life and visitor rhythm. Ottawa International Airport handles the main arrival flow, so hotel choice should balance the centre, transfer time and day-trip plans.

stayOverview: Start with City centre for the easiest first Ottawa stay, then compare Old Town and Waterfront when price, nightlife, quieter evenings or transfer timing matter more than being beside every major sight.
hotelIntro: Ottawa hotel choice is mostly about repeat journeys: use City centre for sightseeing, Old Town for a different local base, and Waterfront or Airport area when views, parking, airport timing or longer stays matter.
rentalCars: Do not rent a car for central Ottawa unless parking and traffic are part of the plan; use one mainly for regional day trips.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose City centre for a first stay because it keeps main sights, restaurants and practical local movement close.

travelTips.title: Airport timing
travelTips.text: Leave extra time for Ottawa International Airport, especially for early flights, late arrivals, traffic or unfamiliar transfer routes.

travelTips.title: Local movement

travelTips.title: Day trips

The governor-general of the Province of Canada designated Kingston as the capital in 1841.
In 1843, a report by the Executive Council recommended Montreal as the capital, as it was a more fortifiable location and commercial centre.
In 1844, the Queen's acceptance of a parliamentary vote moved the capital to Montreal.
The Queen sent a letter to colonial authorities selecting Ottawa as the capital, effective 31 December 1857.
On 1 June 1912, the Grand Trunk Railway opened both the Château Laurier hotel and its neighbouring downtown Union Station.
